Title: write about the transportation in plants related to vascular system?
Question: biology
Answer: Animals have a circulatory system that transports fluids, chemicals, and nutrients around within the animal body. Some plants have an analogous system: the vascular system in vascular plants; trumpet hyphae in bryophytes.

Root hairs are thin-walled extensions of the epidermal cells in roots. They provide increased surface area and thus more efficient absorption of water and minerals. Water and dissolved mineral nutrients enter the plant via two routes. 


Water and selected solutes pass through only the cell membrane of the epidermis of the root hair and then through plasmodesmata on every cell until they reach the xylem: intracellular route (apoplastic). Water and solutes enter the cell wall of the root hair and pass between the wall and plasma membrane until the encounter the endodermis, a layer of cells that they must pass through to enter the xylem: extracellular route (symplastic). 


The endodermis has a strip of water-proof material (containing suberin) known as the Casparian strip that forces water through the endodermal cell and in such a way regulates the amount of water getting to the xylem. Only when water concentrations inside the endodermal cell fall below that of the cortex parenchyma cells does water flow into the endodermis and on into the xylem.
Xylem and Transport 
Xylem is the water transporting tissue in plants that is dead when it reaches functional maturity. Tracheids are long, tapered cells of xylem that have end plates on the cells that contain a great many crossbars. Tracheid walls are festooned with pits. Vessels, an improved form of tracheid, have no (or very few) obstructions (crossbars) on the top or bottom of the cell. The functional diameter of vessels is greater than that of tracheids.

Water is pulled up the xylem by the force of transpiration, water loss from leaves. Mature corn plants can each transpire four gallons of water per week. Transpiration rates in arid-region plants can be even higher. Water molecules are hydrogen bonded to each other. Water lost from the leaves causes diffusion of additional water molecules out of the leaf vein xylem, creating a tug on water molecules along the water columns within the xylem. This "tug" causes water molecules to rise up from the roots to eventually the leaves. The loss of water from the root xylem allows additional water to pass throught the endodermis into the root xylem.

Cohesion is the ability of molecules of the same kind to stick together. Water molecules are polar, having slight positive and negative sides, which causes their cohesion. Inside the xylem, water molecules are in a long chain extending from the roots to the leaves. 

Adhesion is the tendency of molecules of different kinds to stick together. Water sticks to the cellulose molecules in the walls of the xylem, counteracting the force of gravity and aiding the rise of water within the xylem. 

Cohesion-Adhesion Theory
Transpiration exerts a pull on the water column within the xylem. The lost water molecules are replaced by water from the xylem of the leaf veins, causing a tug on water in the xylem. Adhesion of water to the cell walls of the xylem facilitates movement of water upward within the xylem. This combination of cohesive and adhesive forces is referred to as the Cohesion-Adhesion Theory.


Guard Cells Regulate Transpiration
In most environments, the water concentration outside the leaf is less than that inside the leaf, causing a loss of water through openings in the leaf known as stomata (singular = stoma). Guard cells are crescent-shaped cells of the epidermis that flank the stoma and regulate the size of the opening. Together, the guard cells and stoma comprise the stomatal apparatus. Question: Why does the ozone layer deplete?
Answer: Ozone destruction

Chemical factors
Ozone can be destroyed by a number of free radical catalysts, of which the most important are hydroxyl (OH), 
nitric oxide (NO) and atomic chlorine (Cl) and bromine (Br). All of these radicals have both natural and anthropogenic (manmade) sources. At the present time, most of the OH and NO in the stratosphere is of natural origin, but human activity has dramatically increased the chlorine and bromine. These elements are found in certain stable compounds, especially chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which may find their way to the stratosphere and there be liberated by the action of ultraviolet light. Most importantly, the chlorine atoms so generated destroy ozone molecules in a catalytic cycle. In this cycle, a chlorine atom reacts with an ozone molecule, taking an oxygen atom with it (forming ClO) and leaving a normal oxygen molecule. A free oxygen atom then takes away the oxygen from the ClO, and the final result is an oxygen molecule and a chlorine atom, which then reinitiates the cycle. A single chlorine atom would keep on destroying ozone forever were it not for reactions that remove them from this cycle by forming reservoir species such as hydrochloric acid and chlorine nitrate. On a per atom basis, bromine is even more efficient than chlorine at destroying ozone, but there is much less bromine in the atmosphere at present. As a result, both chlorine and bromine contribute significantly to the overall ozone depletion.

Polar stratospheric clouds
The reactivation of atomic chlorine from these reservoir species is normally slow, but is enhanced by the presence of polar stratospheric clouds which appear during Antarctic winters, leading to a strong seasonal cycle in ozone hole formation.

For more info go to http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozone_depletion

Title: A question related to PHP and SQL and all that good stuff...?
Question: Ooooook,

Say I have a table in a database that has several entries. Each entry is a message between users. There are fields like "tousername" and "fromusername" in the table. I'd like to set up a page that would list the current 'conversations' between the user viewing the page and the other users talking to him.

So assuming I select * from the table where the "tousername" equals the user viewing the page, since there are multiple messages to this user from the same person, if I just used a "while()" it would list each entry so every message would show up on this page. I'd like to find a way to select the data from the table but only once for each identical "fromusername", if that makes sense. So that way, each 'conversation' would only appear once on the page and you could see a list of users that you were currently having a conversation with, but without duplicate users because of each row in the table.

Thanks. :p
Answer: SELECT fromusername, tousername
FROM table
GROUP BY tousername, fromusername
HAVING fromusername = 'name of user'
AND status = 'open'

Assuming you have a column, named status, that indicates which conversations are active. That will bring in only the unique pairs you describe.

As described earlier, you could also use DISTINCT:

SELECT DISTINCT tousername, fromusername
FROM table
WHERE fromusername = 'name of user'
AND status = 'open'

The GROUP BY statement is computationally more efficient, but unless you are dealing with millions of records and thousands of concurrent requests, you shouldn't see a difference in performance.

Question: What is antireflective coating?
Answer: an antireflective coating is a very thin film of some material that is put on the surface of a lens.  the thickness of the coating is very important.

the way they work is that light is reflected at any interface between two kinds of materials.  at the air-film interface, some light is reflected, and most passes through.  then at the film-lens interface, some more light is reflected.  now, light is a wave, and so if the thickness of the lens is exactly a quarter of the wavelength of the light, the two reflected waves will cancel each other out.  this actually causes more light of that wavelength to pass through the lens than would pass without the coating.

note that this only works for a particular wavelength.  for glasses and optics the human eye looks through, usually the coating is made to pass more green/yellow light, since this is where the eye is more sensitive.  this causes the red and blue ends of the spectrum to appear to be brighter and is what gives anti-reflective coatings their characteristic purplish color.

These gifts are considered public property and should be turned over to the state.  \n\nUsually, gifts are not taxable income. the amount to be spent are limited, depending on the funds that are available for these purpose. Title: Can I take him to court for calling me a lesbian?
Question: I have a roommate who is  like a sister to me.  She and I have known each other since high school.  When I left my husband, hers left her around the same time.  For finacial reasons, and moral support, we moved in together with our daughters, who are about a year apart in age.

Recently, my friend's ex has decided (for custody issues) that she and I are a couple.  While I have many gay friends and have very short hair, I am in no way a lesbian.  He is planning on citing me in the custody case as a reason that his daughter should not be with her mother (There are many other issues, but this is the one that pertains to me specifically).

My question is: Can I take him to court for slandering my name?  and if not, how can I get this guy to stop?  My daughter and my roommate's daughter both hear this crap come from his mouth every weekend when he brings them back from their separate father-daughter weekends. And I'm sick of it.

Any suggestions?
Answer: There is one barrier that makes slander cases difficult. A 'well-known' attorney explained this to me a few years ago... you have to prove malicious intent.

As was explained to me, someone making false, negative statements about you isn't enough for a slander case. First there has to be harm done - there was in this case, there has to be some sort of loss - this could be as simple as loss of reputation and last, the offender must have been purposely trying to harm you (malicious intent).

Malicious intent is supposedly the hardest part to prove.

I would say that in your case, you would have a rather easy time proving malicious intent because the offender has a clear motivate to attempt to smear your reputation.

Btw, most attorneys require a large 'down payment' for slander cases... anywhere from 5 to 10k.

Question: how does a touch light work, is the person touching the light acting as the ground?
Answer: Touch-sensitive lamps almost always use a  property of the human body -- its capacitance. The word "capacitance" has as its root the word "capacity" -- capacitance is the capacity an object has to hold electrons. The lamp, when standing by itself on a table, has a certain capacitance. This means that if a circuit tried to charge the lamp with electrons, it would take a certain number to "fill it." When you touch the lamp, your body adds to its capacity. It takes more electrons to fill you and the lamp, and the circuit detects that difference. It is even possible to buy little plug-in boxes that can turn any lamp into a touch-sensitive lamp. They work on the same principle.

Question: I would like to know can i be exposed to hepatitis c?
Answer: In truth, the risk of transmission to co-workers or other household members seems to be quite low, and even sexual transmission is rare. The CDC recommends the use of sexual prophylactics by anyone infected with hepatitis C or any other sexually transmissible disease, but common contact is not dangerous. While it should be kept in mind that there is no known mode of transmission for approximately 10% of cases, this should not be taken as a statement that it can be easily casually acquired. Routine precautions around blood, and avoiding the sharing of toothbrushes, razors, and other personal items should provide adequate protection.



A number of agents can cause hepatitis, including infectious diseases, chemical poisons, drugs and alcohol. Hepatitis C is a contagious viral disease that leads to serious, permanent liver damage, and in many cases, death.
 IV drug users represent the largest single risk group.  Sexual contact has been clearly identified as a means of transmitting hepatitis C.  Household contact with another household member that has hepatitis C has also been strongly implicated, and this, in combination with heterosexual exposure, is believed to be responsible for approximately 13% of all infections.  Around 2% of all cases of hepatitis C are thought to be contracted through the occupational risk (needle-stick injuries, blood spills, etc) involved with the health care profession.

Prisoners have enormous incidence of infection - rates reported in some California prisons exceed 80%, with certain institutions reporting nearly 100% of their prisoners infected.

Some skin piercing practices, notably tattooing, body piercing, and acupuncture, have contributed significantly to the spread of HCV, particularly in less industrialized nations. Tattooing in particular poses a serious risk. Even in the presence of good sterilization, studies have suggested that the ink used in tattooing can become contaminated and transmit the virus.

Cocaine users have an abnormally high risk of infection due to the fact that they frequently share snorting straws, which may have small amounts of blood-carrying mucous on them. 

Less obvious, specialized risk factors have been identified resulting from indirect exposures to blood - including manicures, shared toothbrushes and razors, and straight razors in barber shops.

In many surveys, about a third of people who are alcoholics are also infected with the HCV virus.

Question: how many miles long and wide is atlantic ocean?
Answer: The Atlantic Ocean is the second largest of the world's five oceans (after the Pacific Ocean, but larger than the Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean, and Arctic Ocean).

Total Area: total: 76.762 million sq km

It is slightly less than 6.5 times the size of the US

lowest point: Milwaukee Deep in the Puerto Rico Trench -8,605 m 
highest point: sea level 0 m

Extent and Seas

The Atlantic Ocean extends in an S shape from the arctic to the antarctic regions between North and South America on the west and Europe and Africa on the east. It is connected with the Arctic Ocean by the Greenland Sea and Smith Sound; with the Pacific Ocean by Drake Passage, the Straits of Magellan, and the Panama Canal; and with the Indian Ocean by the Suez Canal and the expanse between Africa and Antarctica. The shortest distance across the Atlantic Ocean (c.1,600 mi/2,575 km) is between SW Senegal, W Africa, and NE Brazil, E South America. The principal arms of the Atlantic Ocean are Hudson and Baffin bays, the Gulf of Mexico, and the Caribbean Sea in the west; the Baltic, North, Mediterranean, and Black seas in the east; and the Weddell Sea in the south. More large rivers, including the Mississippi, the Congo, and the Amazon, drain into the Atlantic than into any other ocean.

Ocean Floor

The floor of the Atlantic has an average depth of c.12,000 ft (3,660 m). It is separated from that of the Arctic Ocean by a submarine ridge extending from SE Greenland to N Scotland; part of the floor (c.3,000 ft/910 m deep) is known as “telegraph plateau” because of the network of cables laid there. A shallow submarine ridge across the Strait of Gibraltar separates the Mediterranean basin from the Atlantic and limits the exchange of water between the two bodies. The Mid-Atlantic Ridge (c.300–600 mi/480–970 km wide), a submarine mountain range extending c.10,000 mi (16,100 km) from Iceland to near the Antarctic Circle, generally follows the trend of the coastlines of the continents. It rises to an average height of c.10,000 ft (3,050 m), and a few peaks emerge as islands. The ridge, which is the center of volcanic activity and earthquakes, has a great rift that is constantly widening (see seafloor spreading) and filling with molten rock from the earth's interior. As a result the Western Hemisphere and Europe and Africa are moving away from each other. The Mid-Atlantic Ridge divides the floor of the Atlantic Ocean into eastern and western sections that are composed of a series of deep-sea basins (abyssal plains). The greatest depth (c.28,000 ft/8,530 m) is the Milwaukee Deep, in the Puerto Rico Trench, N of Puerto Rico. Scientific knowledge of the ocean floor dates from the Challenger expedition (1872–76).

Title: what are the activites done by farmers in rural area ??
Question: hint i want a good brief answer
Answer: Farming.

Small farms: everything.  The work literally never ends.  Tilling, planting, fertilizing, watering, harvesting, selling, repeat as many times per season as the climate and crops permit. 

In rural Utah, watering is the critical factor, as everything is run on irrigation systems.  People move pipe or repair pipe quite a bit.  For really small farms, they'll usually grow a few acres of alfalfa for their own animals and to share.  So, there are three or so crops a year of that, which includes bailing and stacking the hay.  

If the farm has animals, they come first.  Always.  My first job was working on a small horse ranch in Utah, where we'd first attend to the animals needs, then go paint a barn, repair a machine, cut thistle in the pasture, burn weeds in the irrigation ditches, or whatever else was pressing.

Large farms: they're more like corporations than old-style farming.  People would have jobs broken down, computers run and manage everything, planes do the fertilizing, the tractors automate much of the work.

What is toxoplasmosis?

A single-celled parasite called Toxoplasma gondii causes a disease known as toxoplasmosis. While the parasite is found throughout the world, more than 60 million people in the United States may be infected with the Toxoplasma parasite. Of those who are infected, very few have symptoms because a healthy person's immune system usually keeps the parasite from causing illness. However, pregnant women and individuals who have compromised immune systems should be cautious; for them, a Toxoplasma infection could cause serious health problems.


How do people get toxoplasmosis?

A Toxoplasma infection occurs by:

    * Accidentally swallowing cat feces from a Toxoplasma-infected cat that is shedding the organism in its feces. This might happen if you were to accidentally touch your hands to your mouth after gardening, cleaning a cat's litter box, or touching anything that has come into contact with cat feces. Eating contaminated raw or partly cooked meat, especially pork, lamb, or venison; by touching your hands to your mouth after handling undercooked meat.
    * Contaminating food with knives, utensils, cutting boards and other foods that have had contact with raw meat.
    * Drinking water contaminated with Toxoplasma.
    * Receiving an infected organ transplant or blood transfusion, though this is rare. 


What are the symptoms of toxoplasmosis?

Symptoms of the infection vary.

    * Most people who become infected with Toxoplasma are not aware of it.
    * Some people who have toxoplasmosis may feel as if they have the "flu" with swollen lymph glands or muscle aches and pains that last for a month or more.
    * Severe toxoplasmosis, causing damage to the brain, eyes, or other organs, can develop from an acute Toxoplasma infection or one that had occurred earlier in life and is now reactivated. Severe cases are more likely in individuals who have weak immune systems, though occasionally, even persons with healthy immune systems may experience eye damage from toxoplasmosis.
    * Most infants who are infected while still in the womb have no symptoms at birth, but they may develop symptoms later in life. A small percentage of infected newborns have serious eye or brain damage at birth. 


Who is at risk for developing severe toxoplasmosis?

People who are most likely to develop severe toxoplasmosis include:

    * Infants born to mothers who became infected with Toxoplasma for the first time during or just before pregnancy.
    * Persons with severely weakened immune systems, such as individuals with HIV/AIDS, those taking certain types of chemotherapy, and those who have recently received an organ transplant. 


What should I do if I think I am at risk for severe toxoplasmosis?

If you are planning to become pregnant, your health care provider may test you for Toxoplasma. If the test is positive it means you have already been infected sometime in your life. There usually is little need to worry about passing the infection to your baby. If the test is negative, take necessary precautions to avoid infection (See below).

If you have a weakened immune system, ask your doctor about having your blood tested for Toxopla

Title: how is caffeine extracted using chloroform?
Question: what are the different mehtods of extracting caffeine from tea? 
by using chloroform, how sure can i be that the results i collected are truely chloroform?
Answer: To separate caffeine, you could use HPLC, LC, GC, or TLC, which are all chromatography techniques. 

If you do a physical separation, a polar organic solvent would do nicely.

To make sure that you are actually extracting the chloroform, suspend the separatory funnel on a ring off of a ring stand. Wait 10 mins. You'll see two layers, a top layer and bottom layer.

Chloroform has a density of 1.48 g/mL and water has a density of 1 g/mL, so the chloroform will be the bottom layer. Use the sep funnel to recover all the chloroform. At the end, I'd run saturated sodium chloride through the chloroform and separate that, to clear any nonorganics from the chloroform.

After that, you can put the chloroform on a rotavap or do TLC to see if you have caffeine and caffeine only (doubtful)

Title: Monarchs and Milkweed question?
Question: Apparently, Monarch butterfly caterpillars are poisonous to  most would be predators because of the protection conferred upon them due to feeding on milkweed.  If it is correct that Monarch butterflies' survival has been enhanced by this selective adaptation (by their larvae being able to tolerate the toxins in milkweed), and this gave them a competitive advantage in the natural world, then why aren't milkweeds crawling with all sorts of other species of caterpillars gaining similar protection?  In other words, why did only Monarch caterpillars hit on this means of protection from predation, when other butterflies and their larvae could have also adapted to milkweed?  If the Monarch butterly gained this tolerance to milkweed through a chance mutation, then why did chance favour *only* the Monarch butterfly and not other butterflies..?
Answer: It's not that they're poisonous but they taste very bitter because they sequester certain chemicals from milkweed. Once a young bird eats one monarch, it never eats another. And actually not all monarchs taste that bitter - but enough to eventually convince most birds to look elsewhere. \n\nThe ability of insects to detoxify or sequester plant chemicals is not a random mutation or even a fixed thing. The plant made the chemicals to deter insect feeding (that is, plants with bitter tasting foliage survived when others did not, so now most of the plant population is bitter). Insects then evolved methods to detoxify these chemicals (that is, the caterpillars that could stomach the taste survived and the genes that allowed this behavior multiplied in the population). The process is known as coevolution and takes millennia. Insects are quite often specific to just one type of plant - they grow up together (evolutionarily speaking) and are constantly changing but at a rate we humans can not readily see.

Title: Neighbor keeps opening gates to my driveway saying it's her land and we cannot close the gates?
Question: My neighbor who is mentally ill is claiming that our driveway is part of her property.  We have been closing our gates for the last couple of weeks to keep her vicious dog out so that our grandchildren can play in the yard without fear of getting bitten.   The neighbor will come right behind us everytime we close the gate and open it back up yelling and cussing saying it's her land and we cannot close the gates.  What kind of action can I take against this woman?  I cannot sleepl, eat or have peace of mind for fear of her hurting me or my family.
Answer: First you really need to make sure that the gates are on your land and that both your Deed and hers do not contain any type of easement, right of ingress or egress, covenant blah blah that entitles her to do this.  Don't assume anything. You probably have your Deed in your files, and you can look at hers for free at the clerk or recorders office.  Many people are amazed to find that their Deed does have one of the above.  

Once you are certain she does not have this right, you can file a complaint in Municipal Court against her.  Chain and padlock the gate while you wait for your court date.  If she keeps it up after you go to court and win, you can probably have her arrested.  At the very least, the police will have to deal with her because you will have an order or decision.  If she gets herself arrested, and she is truly "mentally ill" as you say, there is a chance that she will be remanded for observation.

"We have called the police, 911 and the local dhhr and the humane society and NO ONE will do anything."   

Of course not. The police don't settle Deed issues, she hasn't done anything crazy enough for dhhr to get involved, and the dog hasn't been ruled vicious.  You are going about this all the wrong way, and all you are doing is frustrating yourself.  You are asking people to do things that are not in their power to do.

You need to first check the Deeds and proceed with a complaint filed in Municipal Court against her if you are truly in the right as per your Deeds. Anything less is just going to generate more frustration on your part.

Question: Should coal power continue to be used?
Answer: Well, currently all technologies have their drawback.  I'll go into detail what's up and why:

Nuclear fission - older LWR (light water reactors) are inefficient.  They use less and produce more waste as compared to the newer models using heavy water and sodium cooled reactors.  New generations of nuclear fuel are providing greater efficiencies.  I believe the best would had been the Integral Fast Reactor.  This would had provided proliferation resistant means of producing power.  Waste would had been sorted out with their pyroprocessing methods, and stuff that would be buried would have a half life of no more than 100 years.  It could use up LWR waste and other wastes from lesser efficient breeder reactors to produce power indefinitely.  It could convert at most 20% of waste back to fuel, and reuse.  But with the whole process, the waste leaving would be completely free of actinides and other long lasting radioactive materials.  So, nuclear fission would had been my favorite, if there wasn't such a public outcry for the source.  Until public opinion changes, there will not be any new sources in the US for a while.  Additionally, cost overruns of power plant production (because of a lot of safety mechanisms needed) would deter a lot of investors.

Natural Gas - you know gas.  It's gaining a foothold in the US.  Technologies are becoming more efficient and cleaner.

Nuclear Fusion - Something for the future, but until it's a proven technology, we can't live off of pipe dreams.

Coal - ah, coal.  It is the current favorite source of power in the US.  There are more advanced power plants called coal gasification power plants which uses scrubbers and other means of cleaning up the air.  This is slated to be replaced by natural gas by DOE's estimates.

Wind, Geothermal, and other sources - 
Wind requires expensive equipment that could alter the landscape.  Again, go check on the DOE's website, but they require many windmills to achieve what one powerplant can.  Geothermal requires hot sources in the earth.  Yosemite could be one, if it wasn't preserved.  Look at iceland for that. Solar is expensive and dependant of climate conditions.  It is better in the desert, but in cities with varying climates, we are dependant on a consistant power source.  Tidal sources of energy could be feasible if it didn't alter marine life ecosystems.  Currently it's a newer source of energy.  Scientists haven't perfected the technology to provide a competative means of power source.

My conclusion:
Yes I think coal should be continue to be used for the moment.  Currently, we cannot just change from one source to another because of current technologies and public perception.  There is a great market for this source of power - it won't dissapear in an instant until there are rivalling technologies that could provide comparable rates.  In the end, $$ are the deciding factor between the feasability of one source versus another.

Question: In financial terms what is a Tender Offer?
Answer: Tender offer is a corporate finance term that typically refers to a public, open offer (usually announced in a newspaper advertisement) by an entity to all stockholders of a publicly traded corporation to tender their stock for sale at a specified price for a specified time, subject to the tendering of a minimum and maximum number of shares. In the United States, tender offers are regulated by the Williams Act.\n\nTo induce the shareholders of the target company to sell, the acquiror's offer price usually includes a premium over the current market price of the target company's shares. For example, if a target corporation's stock were trading at a value of $1/share, an acquiror might offer $1.15/share to its shareholders on the condition that 51% of shareholders agree. Cash or other securities may be offered to the target company's shareholders as consideration, although a tender offer in which securities are offered as consideration is generally referred to as an "exchange offer."-

Question: Why is the sky blue and grass green?
Answer: 1. Why the sky is blue.
When light passes through a medium with molecules much smaller than the wavelength, it is scattered. You can understand it so: the light begins by going as a beam "forward". It gets absorbed for a moment by a molecule and then emitted again in whatever direction. This effect is more effective when the wavelength is shorter. Blue light has a wavelength ~2 times shorter than red light and gets scattered 16 times as effectively. So the beam coming directly from the sun is deprived of blue =>thus it is yellow (or red if it is sunset and it has passed a thick layer of atmosphere (geometry)). From all other directions we see the light that was going towards other points on the Earth. The yellows and reds went on and the blue was sent in other directions, including towards us.

2. Why the grass is green.
Green plants use light to make food. The light is absorbed by chlorophyll (two types of it, too and a bit different, but no matter). Chlorophyll absorbs violet, blue, orange and red light. What we see is what was not absorbed, but reflected. If you take the aforementioned colours out of the white light spectrum, you get a mixtureof green and yellow. And green is the colour our eyes see best. Thus - green grass.

Title: what is the definition of symbolic racism?
Question: I am looking for the dictionary definition of Symbolic Racism. I am studying this concept in social science.

Title: Who designed the baseball diamond?
Question: How did he come up with the length of the base paths?
Answer: The basic layout of the diamond has been little changed since the original Knickerbocker Rules of the 1840s. The distance between bases was already established as 90 feet, which it remains to this day. Through trial and error, 90 feet had been settled upon as the optimal distance. 100 feet would have given too much advantage to the defense, and 80 feet too much to the offense. As athleticism has improved on both sides of the equation, 90 feet remains the appropriate balance between hitting and fielding, as it continues to provide frequent tests between the speed of a batter-runner and the throwing arm of a fielder.

The rules consist of twenty general guidelines to the rules of baseball. The organization for which the guidelines were drawn up was the early 1840s New York ball club called the Knickerbockers.

Many of the rules, formalized by Alexander Cartwright on September 23, 1845, were derived from earlier sources, but their compilation by the Knickerbocker Club provided a basis for modern adult organized baseball, in contrast to the various schoolyard ball games that had been around for generations previous.

Question: What is emphysema and what are its causes?
Answer: Q. What is Emphysema?
FAQ

From Stacey Lloyd,
Your Guide to Lung Diseases.

A.

Emphysema is a lung disease in which the walls of the alveoli (air sacs) in the lungs fracture or burst. As these alveoli break, the remaining alveoli become enlarged to make up for the loss. This results in a fewer number of alveoli, with many enlarged. 
When alveoli are enlarged, they loose their elasticity. A loss of elasticity in the alveoli results in the inability to eliminate air from the lungs. Therefore, patients must use force (energy) to expel this air. 

Furthermore, the loss of elasticity in the lungs affects the smaller bronchial tubes. To push air out of the bronchial tubes, a higher pressure must be developed inside the chest. 

This higher pressure tends to collapse the smaller bronchial tubes, making it even more difficult to empty air from the alveoli. 
Coughing becomes very difficult and ineffective in expelling mucus, leaving the lungs more susceptible to lung infections, such as pneumonia. 

( http://lungdiseases.about.com/od/emphysema/f/emphysema_expl.htm )

What causes emphysema?
Emphysema can be caused by one or a combination of these things:

Cigarette smoking: Most cases of emphsyema are caused by cigarette smoking. Cigarette smoke reaches deep into the lungs and causes permanent damage. If you have emphysema from cigarettes, the best way to stop your lung damage is to quit smoking as soon as possible. It's never too late to quit smoking. 
Alpha-1 Antitrypsin deficiency: Some people have emphsyema because of a rare genetic disorder called Alpha-1 Antitrypsin deficiency. People with Alpha-1 are missing an enzyme that protects their lungs. Some people with Alpha-1 deficiency get emphysema without ever having smoked. Other people get emphsyema from the combination of smoking and having Alpha-1 deficiency. 
Air pollution: There is some evidence that air pollution can contribute to people getting emphysema, especially if the person also smokes. ( http://www.lung.ca/diseases-maladies/a-z/emphysema-emphyseme/index_e.php#causes )

Question: how can u cure pain of arthritis?
Answer: If you haven't had a clinical diagnosis, don't give up on the possibility that your pain might not be arthritis. My husband had a variety of symptoms, one of which was joint and bone pain. The doctors tested him for rhumatoid, but the results came back negative. It turned out that he had celiac disease. Celiac primarily impacts the digestive system, but advanced cases of the disease get all sorts of autoimmune problems and nutrient deficiencies - one of which is bone and joint pain. Once he quit getting gluten in his diet his pain completely went away. 

If he gets a gluten infraction the pain will return. We had that last summer when they had cookouts at work pretty regularly for several weeks in a row. He was careful to select foods that were gluten free, but he kept getting a reaction each time. Since he could find no initial cause, he figured he just had a mild viral infection. By the end of two weeks he had terrible bone and joint pain. We finally discovered that Kingsford charcoal uses gluten as a binding agent in their bricketts. The cookouts were with Kingsford. Kingsford stated that the gluten would burn up completely and couldn't contaminate the food; however, my husband's body showed them to be wrong. He quite eating the grilled foods and his symptoms subsided in just a few days. We have come arcross several other celiacs since then who said they had the same problem with Kingsford.

So, if your doctor hasn't difinitively gotten test results that prove arthritis, do a bit of research to see what conditions have this pain as a symptom.

Good luck.

Question: As a deaf college graduate, is it hard to get an entry level position in an investment firm?
Answer: Yeah, the law protects you.  That sounds great.  Now for the reality check.  Most 'entry level' investment jobs involve lots of phone calls with potential clients.  If you're not 100% adept at phone etiquette, you probably couldn't get that position, and I don't think the technology that you'd be using as a deaf person has yet reached the stage where that would be the case.  So, I think you'd be realistically limited from a lot of the entry level jobs.

Since you're effectively barred from those jobs, you're stuck going after the few other entry level jobs in research, etc.  Now for the good news.  Those phone jobs are crappy jobs anyway.  That's where most new college grads get stuck, and it's miserable, and most of them give up within a year.  Instead, you're stuck with the better jobs.  Sure, they're going to be harder to get, cuz there are fewer of them, and many firms aren't organized to take entry level people in any other function.  But this will just assure you that you'll keep looking until you find a good position.  So, with that limitation, yes, it is hard for anyone to get one of those good entry level positions.  You'll just have to persevere.  That's a good thing because you won't make it in the investment world unless you have a lot of perseverence anyway.

By the way, I'd suggest playing to your strengths.  Consider what areas of the investment business you'd be strongest at, and which areas you'd be weakest in, and focus your attention on your strengths.  If you're a good writer and researcher, apply for positions with research firms or publishers.  If you're better at portfolio management, perhaps mutual funds would be a good direction to pursue.  If you're into sales, I suppose I'd look toward the big brokerage firms.  

Best of luck to you.

Question: what is the relation of the mass of stars to its evolution?
Answer: Star formation occurs in molecular clouds, large regions of high density in the interstellar medium (though still less dense than the inside of an earthly vacuum chamber). Star formation begins with gravitational instability inside those clouds, often triggered by shockwaves from supernovae or collision of two galaxies (as in a starburst galaxy). High mass stars powerfully illuminate the clouds from which they formed. One example of such a nebula is the Orion Nebula.

Stars spend about 90% of their lifetime fusing hydrogen to produce helium in high-temperature and high-pressure reactions near the core. Such stars are said to be on the main sequence.

Small stars (called red dwarfs) burn their fuel very slowly and last tens to hundreds of billions of years. At the end of their lives, they simply become dimmer and dimmer, fading into black dwarfs. However, since the lifespan of such stars is greater than the current age of the universe (13.7 billion years), no black dwarfs exist yet.

As most stars exhaust their supply of hydrogen, their outer layers expand and cool to form a red giant. In about 5 billion years, when the Sun is a red giant, it will be so large that it will consume both Mercury and Venus. Eventually the core is compressed enough to start helium fusion, and the star heats up and contracts. Larger stars will also fuse heavier elements, all the way to iron, which is the end point of the process. Since iron nuclei are more tightly bound than any heavier nuclei, they cannot be fused to release energy. Likewise, since they are more tightly bound than all lighter nuclei, energy cannot be released by fission. In old, very massive stars, a large core of inert iron will accumulate in the center of the star.

An average-size star will then shed its outer layers as a planetary nebula. The core that remains will be a tiny ball of degenerate matter not massive enough for further fusion to take place, supported only by degeneracy pressure, called a white dwarf. These too will fade into black dwarfs over very long stretches of time.

 
The Crab Nebula, remnants of a supernova which occurred around 1050 AD.In larger stars, fusion continues until an iron core accumulates that is too large to be supported by electron degeneracy pressure. This core will suddenly collapse as its electrons are driven into its protons, forming neutrons and neutrinos in a burst of inverse beta decay. The shockwave formed by this sudden collapse causes the rest of the star to explode in a supernova. Supernovae are so bright that they may briefly outshine the star's entire home galaxy. When they occur within the Milky Way, supernovae have historically been observed by naked-eye observers as "new stars" where none existed before. Eventually, most of the matter in a star is blown away by the explosion (forming nebulae such as the Crab Nebula) and what remains will be a neutron star (sometimes a pulsar or X-ray burster) or, in the case of the largest stars, a black hole.

The blown-off outer layers of dying stars include heavy elements which may be recycled during new star formation. These heavy elements allow the formation of rocky planets. The outflow from supernovae and the stellar wind of large stars play an important part in shaping the interstellar medium.

Title: What is advertismen? How do I get rid of it?
Question: I tried to remove by going to add and remove programs,restarted computer as it instructed and it is still listed in add and remove programs. Could this be why Chrysler Golf Challenge graphics are messed up?
Answer: Advertismen is a type of spyware that most anti-spyware programs don't pick up. I can give you directions on how to remove it, but they involve modifying your system registry. Please be very careful when altering your registry and don't modify anything except the file included in the instructions.
   1. Close ALL Internet Explorer, Firefox, etc. windows.
   2. Click on start, then click on "Run..." and type:   regedit and click "ok"
   3. On the left side click "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE" then SOFTWARE> Microsoft> Windows NT> CurrentVersion> Windows
   4. On the right-hand side you should see a String called “AppInit_DLLs” with a value of “pushow*.dll” where * is a random number.
   5. Right-click on this String and click Delete and then exit regedit.
   6. Go to "My Computer" and open "C:\windows\system32\"
   7. In that folder there is a file called "pushow*.dll," where * is the random number you saw above. Delete all pushow*.dll files.

That's all you need to do to remove the program. In the future, be careful about downloading things when you're not sure what they are. If you don't already have an anti-spyware program, I suggest you download adaware: http://www.lavasoft.de/software/adaware/

Title: I have a pimple on my chin, big! but it isn't like a pimple, its like a inside lump.swollen it did go now?
Question: but, i thought it was a spider bit but i dont think so,its like ingrow,big lump. , have u ever got this?? 
, what should i do to make it go away ,,,fast...how did i get this!!!!!!
Answer: Okay there are several possibilities here.  One is cystic acne, HOWEVER, if you have not had cystic acne before it would be very unusual for it to start now and for you to have only one spot effected! (fyi, cystic acne is aka underground pimples and do not come to a "head" easily and often leave scars).  Two, this could be an ingrown hair. This is much more common in males who shave but can occur in females as well. The hair literally has been covered with epidermis (top layer of skin) and is growing inward which causes a local inflammatory reaction/infection.  Third, an abscess caused by a local infection.  Now, to be technically correct all of the above, including a basic pimple, are abscesses (pus filled lesions). I am differentiating by cause be it a cystic pimple, ingrown hair or secondary infection (i.e. a scratch).

Treatment: "Let the 'evil' humours out!" 
In other words..."release the pus!"  Most teenagers are adept at this by squeezing their 'zits,' but the type of lesion/lump you have will not simply erupt with squeezing. If anything, you risk making it worse! So what do you do? Well, you can try: 
1) Direct heat with a wash cloth soaked in the hottest water you can stand without burning yourself and an astringent such as Witch Hazel.  This will, hopefully, bring the lesion to a 'head' (a whitish or thin dome on top) at which point it is ready for extruding (i.e. a good squeeze to release the pus)!) 2) Apply antibiotic cream or ointment 3 times a day along with a secondary antibiotic like Oxy 10 (this will hopefully reduce the size by fighting the infection). 3) Finally, IF the lump is indeed pus filled and not simple induration (inflammatory response that precedes the pus stage) you need it drained. IF you are lucky and step number one allowed you to get rid of the pus (that white/yellow nasty stuff that you get out of pimples) then, Great! BUT, if you have an ingrown hair or the secondary infection then you will need 'surgical' drainage and treatment of the underlying problem. In other words, a doctor needs to lance the lump with a scalpel. DON'T STRESS! This is done with a bit of local anesthetic and a quick stab with a small surgical blade which releases the pus and you instantly feel much better! You may need oral antibiotics such as cephalexin or sulfa or clindamycin or doxicycline as well as topical (skin applied) antibiotics to treat the infection. The doctor may remove the ingrown hair if that is the cause.

Bottom line: IF the lump does NOT come to a head or does not recede with topical treatment then you need to see your doctor for definitive care. Don't stress! The treatment is FAR better than the alternative of a worsened infection that could, RARELY, lead to admission to the hospital for major IV antibiotics and surgery.  Treat it early and aggressively!

ALSO, Since I know that people with pimples may be reading this...PLEASE be careful in squeezing pimples in the 'T' zone. This is the area from the tip of your nose to the forehead from between your eyebrows! The drainage system of this area leads DIRECTLY toward your brain!  I am not joking in relating the following anecdote: I had a patient DIE of a pimple! He squeezed one in this T zone and the infection spread to his brain and he died of cerebritis (brain infection) despite aggressive treatment!

USE topical antibiotics or see your doctor if you have a 'zit' that gets bigger in this 'T' Zone or has worsened redness of the surrounding skin (aka Cellulitis).

Good Luck!

Greg M.D.

Title: if you have had negative items deleted off your credit report?
Question: What did you do to do it?
How many disput letters did it take?

did any tatic help you more than others?
Answer: Yes, I have helped many, many people do this.  First know that the bureau must verify any debt you dispute.  If they can not verify it, it must be deleted.  They have 30 days to do this.

With 7 years in the credit business, I recommend disputing them all at the same time, as you will likely need to go through several rounds of letters to get what you want done. If something is blatently wrong with your credit report, call the bureau after they write back and refuse to remove it. Go up the food chain until a manager agrees to remove or amend the incorrect info on the spot. Don't buy into their speach about re-disputing it - but make sure you have provided the information necessary by mail already to correct the error. It will not help you to insist on something being removed if you have not provided verificaiton on why.

When you mail in the dispute letter, mail in as much information as possible with it. If your verification is a bankruptcy, send in all the pages to your petition and tab the important pages for them to review.

Also mail in a copy of an electric bill and a copy of your ID to avoid any delays. See the FTC web's site for your specific rights with collectors and debt reporting:

http://www.ftc.gov/

If your problem is directly with the creditors, write to them ONE time. If they do not remove incorrect information, write to your state's attorney general's office and the FTC. This will get you the results you seek if you are in the right.

If this is a collection agency problem, write to the same people plus the ACA at www.acainternational.org. Collection agencies are generally slime, so know your rights before you call them. See your rights here:

http://www.ftc.gov/bcp/conline/edcams/credit/index.html

If you have legit items that are bad, dispute them also. If they can not be verified, they must be deleted. It is not your responsibility to prove they are inaccurate, it is the credit bureaus who must demonstrate they are.

Hope this helps!

Title: why is the sky blue?
Question: it's the age old question....
Answer: The sky appears blue because the gases(mainly nitrogen and oxygen) present in our atmosphere vibrate at a specific frequency.  From the light that we can see, ie.. blue, green, red, yellow...etc, the the higher frequency colors are absorbed more by the atmosphere than the lower frequency(actually they're scattered, they still make it to us but indirectly whereas the yellowish color of the sun is more direct).  So blue, green, and violet(violet having the shortest wavelength) are absorbed by the atmosphere, while red, yellow and orange are allowed through.   The color of blue that we perceive the sky varies from day to day based on the content of gases present and the frequency that they vibrate.  It works the same way as light passing through a blue balloon, except in this case the balloon is our atmosphere.

Question: who was Dr.Clopton Havers?

1655?-1702

English physician who is known for his study of bone structure and growth, as well as his book Osteologia Nova, which was the first publication to describe bone structure in great detail. Title: What about better brake lights?
Question: measure brake cylinder pressure | to microcontroller

standard brake light set ensures standard reliable function

additionally

"tracer" brake light set 1-4

tracer light set strobes when anti-lock function enabled

or

brake cylinder 'over'pressure
Answer: In automitive engineering it is often hard to define "better" especially in a competitive litigeous world.  As you mention, your brake lights are meant to alert the driver behind you.  Without a considerable amount of education, I think it would be difficult to train other drivers to interpret what you are doing with your brakes.  When accidents are caused it may become the burdon of the person braking to prove they did not cause confusion in a law suit.  If everyone has the same brakes, there should be less (lawyer caused?) confusion.  For example, some drivers merely tap on their brakes to alert a tailgater to back off.  The brake light comes on with little or no real braking action.

However, there is no reason that novel methods of making brake lights more practicable, efficient and reliable should not be adopted.  Modern cars now are required to have brake lights in the rear window as well as at the tail lights; because that places them more at eye level.  Progress is slow but sure.  There is in engineering what is called the "coke bottle" effect.  For many many years Coke used the same small green coke bottle, because it worked!  If you change something that "works" you may solve one proble but create three new problems.  That said Coke did move on to use clear glass Coke bottles and bottles in larger sizes and plastic too.  Each advance may have given them new production headaches while on the learning curve.  I'd encourage you to pursue your novel ideas; but always search for the adverse effects.  Good luck.

Title: how do I get post-operative swelling to reduce without perscription drugs???
Question: My daughter has had cochlear implant surgery and is unable to be activated because the surgery site is still too swollen.  I am looking for methods to reduce the swelling in order for her to get activated.
Answer: There are a couple ways to do this, but they won't be cure-alls; just helps.  

Ibuprofen (Advil) is an NSAID, or a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug.  As the description says, it has anti-inflammatory (anti-swelling) properties, and it will help with pain.  More than likely, any other meds you are giving her do not contain ibuprofen or aspirin, but if they do, I wouldn't use this.

Benadryl (Diphenhydramine) has properties which stop the body from reacting to irritants; that's why they use it for rashes, poison ivy, etc.  This would help as well, although it'll probably make her tired.  Diphenhydramine is the exact same drug used in the sleep aid Sominex.  (Yeah, Benadryl and Sominex are the same drug - rip off, eh?  Buy whichever is cheaper...actually, buy the cheap-o generics if they're available -- there really is no difference whatsoever.)

That's about all I can think of over the counter.  Other people may have good ideas as well, and I'd trust the advice of your doctor over anything you read on here.

I'd use coldpacks, but I'd stay away from using heat; it dilates the blood vessels and may make the pain worse.  Heat is best for muscular pain.

P.S. - Her age matters, too.  If we're talking about an infant here, I would go ONLY by the advice of your doctor.

Click the "Messenger" menu in Yahoo! Messenger and select "Connection Preferences."
Enable the "Use proxies" option.

Is it tacky to ask, "Does this position include receptionist duties?".  The prospective is asking you questions, shouldn't you as well? Or do you wait for the interview to find out...?
Answer: Perfectly logical for you to ask questions about the job duties.  It is also a good idea to ask for a copy of your Job Description.  Now they might not allow you to have the job description at the interview stage, but once you are offered the position, you have every right to ask them to provide you with this.  I've interviewed people for the past 15 years and I'm actually concerned when people don't ask questions.  Better to find out prior to your first day what is expected of you.  You can ask directly "Does this position include receptionist duties?" or "What is a typical day like for the position?"  

I like to tell people to not think of it as you are interviewing for the company, but you are the one doing the interview OF the company.  You have knowledge, skills and abilities that they are looking to purchase from you in the form of a salary - but if you are not happy with their working environment, you'll take those knowledge, skills and abilities to the company down the street. 

Good Luck!!

Question: What rhymes with canvas?
Answer: How to go about finding good rhymes:

To get a "perfect rhyme" you would have to exactly match all the sounds from the accented vowel to the end of the word.  That is, any perfect rhyme would have to end with "-anvas" (at least in sound, if not in spelling).
http://www.bartleby.com/61/83/P0188300.html

In this case there is no such PERFECT rhyme (something that is much more often the case than people realize).  But you can do rather well at finding a "NEAR rhyme" by matching the VOWEL sounds of these syllables ('full assonance'), ending with the same consonant sound ('final consonance') [or perhaps something close] and matching, or coming as close as possible to matching the remaining consonants.   In ANY case, the ACCENT of the words must be the same (words ending with an accented "-ASS" will NOT work!)

For the 'near matching' pay attention to sounds that are likely to provide the closest matches:

* /m/ and /ng/ sounds are very close to the /n/ sound (all three are 'nasals'), /d/ and voice /th/ are also reasonably close
* the closest sounds to /v/ are /f/ /b/ an /p/  (all are labials --formed with the lips); /th/ is close (esp the voiced version as in 'there')
* for the final voiceless /s/ you might be able to use the related voiced /z/ sound or the /sh/ sound (these three s-sounds are called 'sibilants')

Adding an extra consonant sound, or deleting one, esp. from a cluster or consecutive sounds may also work.   So for instance, you might omit the n or v, or add an r after the combination.

Finally, for the vowels -- perfect matching is desirable, but sometimes you can use something very close.   Also be sure you pay attention to WHAT the vowel sounds really are, which is NOT the same as looking at the letters!      

In this case 
1)  the a of "can" is the short a of 'cat' ,etc. -- but note that following it with an r changes it to a different sound;  also, since this vowel has the accent, it is likely to be less forgiving of substitutes (such as a short e).
2)  the "a" in "vas" is the unaccented, 'swallowed', sometimes almost non-existent vowel-sound called "schewa" or "schwa" [since that e itself is an instance of the sound].  Short unaccented vowel-sounds like short i and the sound of 'uh' may work but are not identical.

Now which of the possibilities will work may depend on the exact context in which you are using it -- some rhyme-schemes and types of poetry demand very close matching, others are more forgiving (a limerick for instance).    In some poetic contexts you can even play a bit with the pronunciation to make it match better.  AND occasionally a dialectal pronunciation may allow a word to work or work better which otherwise wouldn't.


So, here are some ideas:

iambus
campus, Grampus

Candice
canthus, xanthous
Kansas
ankus
angus
anxious
chancrous
polyandrous
pangus

enchantress  (the final  short e is not a perfect match, but close)

'command us', 'stamp us' and other two-word combinations may work, though notice that the final vowel is a short u, not a schewa.  (Since the final word IS a separate word it takes more accent which prevents the vowel from being 'reduced' all the way to a schewa.) 

IF the dialect you use 'drops' final r's, the following might work:
ambers, cambers
camphors

Sometimes the following words virtually drop the middle syllable, which might make them reasonable matches:
amorous, clamorous, glamorous  (to indicate the shortened version one might write them as "am'rous", etc.)

Question: If killing people is wrong then why do we kill people to show people that killing people is wrong??/?
Answer: In some parts of the US, they have capital punishment. In those places, certain murderers are condemned to be executed by the state. There are two commonly cited reasons for this. First, public knowledge that a death penalty exists and can be administered is supposed to deter would-be murderers from killing.To say it in the easy, first-person way- If I know that I could get punished with death because I kill someone, that will theoretically make me hesitate to kill a person. Secondly, the people of some states are of the opinion that it is less costly to execute a convicted murderer than to keep that person in prison for life, but the calculations as to the cost-efficiency are not conclusive.  The expressed attitude seems to be that once a person has killed, that person cannot be trusted not to kill again and must be removed from society.
In actual practice, the families of murder victims frequently talk about seeking closure, saying that only the death of the murderer will bring them peace.  That seems like revenge to me. rather than a noble social aim.  It is pretty insensitive of me to even discuss such matters.  Can I declare myself morally superior to others and say that it is wrong to seek revenge? I have no such right.  I can only say that the desire for revenge is the driving force behind much of the violence in the world today. I can only say that if we could get away from the idea of revenge, many violent acts would not happen.
I would like to give one last bit of food for thought: when humans act alone and independantly, we do not always take the time to fully justify our morality, but when we act as a society- by making laws- we need to have morals that we can explain.
Thank you for asking an important question.

Question: what is power factor?
Answer: Electric power has two components:

Active power, which produces work.
Reactive power, which is needed to generate magnetic fields required for operation of inductive electrical equipment, but performs no useful work. 
Active power is measured in KW (1000 Watts) 
Reactive power is measured in KVAR (1000 Volt-Amperes Reactive) 
Total power is measured in KVA (1000 Volt-Amperes)

Power Factor is the measure of the relationship between Active and Reactive power at the point of consumption.

Question: what percen of the earth's crust igneous?
Answer: Igneous rocks are formed when molten rock (magma) cools and solidifies, with or without crystallization, either below the surface as intrusive (plutonic) rocks or on the surface as extrusive (volcanic) rocks. This magma can be derived from either the Earth's mantle or pre-existing rocks made molten by extreme temperature and pressure changes. Over 700 types of igneous rocks have been described, most of them formed beneath the surface of the Earth's crust. The word "igneous" is derived from the Latin ignis, meaning "fire".

Igneous rock are classified according to mode of occurrence, texture, chemical composition, and the geometry of the igneous body.

Igneous rocks make up 95% of the Earth's upper crust.

Question: I have a pond in my back yard about 50X18. It is usually 4-5ft deep and the banks are nothing extraordinary, no retaining walls etc. I would like to determine the volume of water for chemical treatment purposes. The formula would be even better. (you might have to dumb it down a bit). Thanks
Answer: If it's an ellipse the area is pi*r1*r2, r1 and r2 being the semimajor and semiminor axes. This is 3.14*25*9 ~= 705 sq. ft. You'll have to estimate the average depth. If it's 4 feet you have 4*705 ~= 2820 cu ft. There are ~7.5 gallons in a cu ft, so that's 7.5*2820 ~= 21200 gallons.

Question: Who owns Best Buy? How long have they been in business?
Answer: Best Buy is a publiclly traded company and is owned by share holders.(NYSE: BBY)

Era 1 -- Humble Beginnings
Milestone: The Journey Begins  
1966 -- Richard Schulze and business partner open the Sound of Music store in St. Paul, Minnesota. 

1967 -- Kencraft Hi-Fi Company and Bergo Company acquired; second and third Sound of Music stores are opened near the University of Minnesota and in downtown Minneapolis. 

1967 -- Sound of Music ends first year with gross sales of $173,000. 

1969 -- Sound of Music stock first traded over the counter as publicly- held company; company enacts first employee stock option plan; three stores opened in the Twin Cities area. 

1970 -- Sound of Music hits the $1 million mark in annual revenues. 

Era 2 -- Growth and Challenge
Milestone: The Tornado Sale  
1972 -- Sound of Music begins sales and installation of 8-track automobile stereos. 

1973 -- Sound of Music facility opens in Edina, Minnesota, featuring a 5,000-square-foot showroom and 3,000-square-foot warehouse; company brings advertising and marketing efforts in-house. 

1974 -- Sound of Music moves into new headquarters in Bloomington, Minnesota. 

1977 -- Sound of Music expands into the Twin Cities suburbs. 

1978 – Sound of Music has nine stores by year end. 

1979 -- Sound of Music expands into video products; first suppliers of video and laser disc equipment include Panasonic, Magnavox, Sony and Sharp. 

1981 -- A tornado hits store in Roseville, Minnesota. Sound of Music responds with a “Tornado Sale,” introducing the idea of low prices in a “no-frills” retail environment. 

1981 -- Stores add photography and home office products, with video equipment and TV’s expanding to all stores; as a measure of the success of the enhanced assortment, stores average $350 in sales per square foot versus an industry average of $150 - $200 per square foot. 

1982 -- Sound of Music holds Second Annual Tornado Sale and embraces a retail philosophy of name-brand, price-and-item sales 

Era 3 -- Forging New Paths
Milestones: Enter the Superstore, What’s in a Name?  
1983 -- Sound of Music’s board of directors approves a new corporate name: Best Buy Co., Inc.; Best Buy opens first superstore in Burnsville, Minnesota, featuring expanded selling space, a wide assortment of discounted brand-name goods, central service, and warehouse distribution; stores begin selling appliances and VCRs. 

1984 -- Consumer Electronics Monthly magazine names Best Buy to its top-10 list of “Consumer Retailers of the Year.” Richard Schulze announces in NARDA News: ‘We’ve taken the stance that we won’t be undersold on any item.” 

1985 -- Best Buy’s initial public offering on the Nasdaq raises $8 million; Best Buy expands the superstore format outside the Twin Cities and opens stores in St. Cloud, Moorhead, and Rochester, Minnesota. 

1986 -- A public stock offering raises $33.6 million, helping finance a 12-store expansion; first stock split (two-for-one) in March; stores begin offering CD’s and an expanded line of photo- equipment. 

1987 -- Best Buy (symbol BBY) debuts on the NYSE with an offering of 8.3 million shares; three-for-two stock split in February; annual sales more than double for the fourth consecutive year, soaring 112%. 

1988 -- Best Buy stores begin selling PCs. 

1989 --– Best Buy unveils a revolutionary “grab-and-go” store format – Concept 2 -- that offers customers pressure-free, non-commissioned shopping in a warehouse-style environment; Best Buy’s brand logo changes to the familiar yellow tag; the new “head-heart- hands” approach increases in-store sales, profits and customer satisfaction 


Era 4 -- Unprecedented Growth
Milestone: A novel concept  
1990 -- Richard Schulze is named Retailer of the Year for the third consecutive year by Consumer Electronics and Audio-Video International magazines. 

1991 -- Best Buy enters the Texas and Chicago markets;

Question: digital video?
Answer: Refers to the capturing, manipulation and storage of video in digital formats. A digital video (DV) camcorder, for example, is a video camera that captures and stores images on a digital medium such as a DAT.....The history of digital video can be helpful in understanding the background of the technology that has had to evolve in order to produce quality reproductions of sound and images. The development of electronic reproduction of sound began at the end of the nineteenth century with the invention of the telephone. By the beginning of the twentieth century, the invention of the phonograph and radio had expanded the applications of electronic sound.

After World War II, electronic motion pictures were found in people's homes through the invention of television. Television used analog technology to produce these pictures with sound. Analog technology requires information representing images and sound to be in a real-time continuous-scale electric signal between sources and receivers. Analog systems have become highly developed and widely used today.

However, digital technology has also become widely used and a cost effective technology. Its roots also go back to the early nineteenth and early twentieth century. Digital technology is the representation of data by a fixed number of discrete points. Originally digital technology was developed for the purpose electronic computation. After World War II, digital computers were available, but they were expensive and difficult to use. This was true until the 1960's when solid state integrated circuits were developed. With this development, computing costs dropped, and computing speed and reliability increased, as well as the use of computers.

With the millions of televisions and VCRs in use today and the commonality of the personal computer, the merging of the controllability of personal computers with the quality images of television was inevitable. This merger can best be described as an evolution of computers and television technology which have united to produce interactive digital video.

Question: Does anyone differentiate between the Investment in Subsidiary and Investment in Associate?
Answer: There are three ways to account for investments - four if you're being really picky. 

1.  A "subsidiary" is where it's parent company owns 50% or more (and has management control).  A subsidiary is consolidated into the parent company's financial statements.  

2.  An "associate" is 20-50% owned, with the parent company not having management control. An associate is reported using equity accounting.

3.  "Cost" accounting is typically used on investments where the parent owns less than 20%.  The investment is reported at the lower of cost or market.  

4. If an investment is held for sale or as inventory, the investment is reported at market.

Title: What made the building of the Panama canal an almost impossible feat?
Question: A. How were the obstacles elliminated?


B. Why was the completion of this massive project which took ten years to build such a big deal when it finally opened?
Answer: A. Various diseases hampered the construction project because many people died.  Yellow fever and Malaria were the most deadly of them, because before the cause of them was discovered (mosquitoes) they didn't know how to treat the disease.

Also the original French plan called for a sea level canal like Suez.  Unfortunately for the French the Panamanian landscape didn't allow them to dig so easily as they did in Suez, and the technology they were using in Panama was the same one as they used in Suez, which was all wrong.

When the US got the rights to build the canal arising from the Hay - Buneau Varilla treat of 1903, they reengineered the plans and decided to go for a lock type canal, rather than a sea level canal.  They based this on a prior study from a French engineer.  They also brought new technology with them, for example Concrete.  Remember we're talking about 1903 here.

Also the US got a hold of the research that a Cuban medic called Carlos Finlay did on Yellow Fever where he discovered that mosquitoes were the vectors causing the disease, and the incubation time needed for the mosquitoes to transfer the disease.

With that the US drained swamps, and they fumigated the entire Canal Zone, along with the Panamanian Cities of Cristobal, Colon and Panama to get rid of the mosquitoes.

B. Actually it wasn't a big deal when the Canal opened in 1914.  It was the smallest story on the front page news.  Remember WWI just broke out in Europe, so the news from the battlefront were more interesting than the first transit of the canal.  By the way it was done by the Steamship Ancon.

Now regarding commerce and the military advantage it gave the US, it was a big deal.  Ships could now shorten the time it took them to go around the Cape of Horns in South America, and also for those ships that had to cross the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa.  The US military could complement their fleets just crossing some vessels through the Canal.  Think about all the savings it brought to commerce, and the possibilites to the military strategists at that time.

Also until 1977 the Panama Canal was controlled by the US Military, not the US Federal Government as some still think.  The office handling the Panama Canal affairs was in the Pentagon, not the Secretary of Commerce.  After 1977 with the new Panama Canal Treaties (they were 3 treaties in one single body) The Neutrality Treaty declared the Panama Canal neutral in all times of wars and crisis, therefore now any ship couldn't be denied the right to go through the Panama Canal.  Although I don't believe that prior to 1977 the US actually denied transit except in WWII for obvious reasons.

Title: SQL GROUP BY clause giving me grief AGAIN!?

SELECT t4_key, year, season, month, day
FROM rw_top40
WHERE year = 97 AND season = '2 - summer'
ORDER BY t4_key, year, season, month, day;

WHERE year = 97

Question: Does atomic tunneling pose a problem in the creation of nanostructures?
Answer: well, to some extent the answer to this question depends largely on the nature of the nanostructure and what its function will be.  in some cases, the tunneling is a problem, but in other cases, the structures are designed specifically to take advantage of tunneling effects.

(i also notice you wrote atomic tunneling - did you mean electron tunneling?  an atom *can* tunnel, theoretically, but because it is a composite object, the probability is extraordinarily low that all of the particles in the atom will tunnel at once.  

also, the particles in the nucleus are very small, very light, and very tightly bound.. as such their tunneling lengths are much smaller than the size of the atom itself.  so while it is possible that the nucleus could be involved in tunneling, it is very unlikely on scales larger than a femtometer, which is much smaller than even a single atom.  so, i will assume you mean electron tunneling, which is what most people talk about.)

anyway, one problem that springs to mind is becoming more and more important in the semiconductor industry.  you may have heard of moore's law, which is an observation that over the lifetime of the integrated circuit industry, the "feature size" or structure size has been halved approximately every 18 months.  this means that transistors and wires shrink, and more and more components get squeezed together on a silicon chip.

tunneling is a problem in this situation since it sets an ultimate limit on how small these features can get.  intel for example is ramping up to create processors with a 45-nanometer feature size by 2007.  these things certainly qualify as nanostructures.

however, once you get under about 10nm or so, the wires and so on will be so closely spaced that electrons will tunnel from one to the other; this could turn a 0 into a 1, which would be a Bad Thing.  a way around this is to design circuits that are so-called "fault-tolerant" but this requires more hardware - which will only buy you a little bit of time, since more hardware offsets the smaller-hardware gain.  so this is a fundamental limit to standard circuits imposed by tunneling.

on the other hand, lots of nanostructures are currently being researched that take advantage of tunneling effects.  there is a whole sub-field of materials/physical science that can be called "single-electron electronics".  this is where one electron is used to represent a bit, rather than the thousands or millions used in normal electronics.

these electronics are typically made out of clusters of atoms called "quantum dots" and a few molecules.  at this size, tunneling effects are the primary source of the functionality of these devices!  people are working on single-electron transistors where an electron tunneling across a nanometer-sized barrier performs the "switching" that makes a transistor useful.  you could google the phrase "coulomb staircase" to see instances of this phenomenon.  

there is a lot of active research in this area - for example, here is the page of a guy in my department, who is working on using gold nanoparticles as the tunneling barrier between two long polymer "wires":  http://www.chem.utoronto.ca/staff/DHIRANI/research.htm

however, at this point the state of the art is pretty primitive - certain building blocks like transistors and single logic gates have been made, but it's difficult to make them into larger functional circuits because they're so damned small.

actually, now that i've written all this i see that you asked about the *creation* of nanostructures.  there are lots of different ways of creating nanostructured materials.  some involve self-assembly, where molecules arrange themselves into nanometer-sized structures because that structure is energetically favorable.  other ways include blasting away at some bulk material with a tightly focused beam (see focused-ion-beam (FIB) etchin

Question: whta is swing in java?
Answer: Swing is a GUI toolkit for Java. Swing is one part of the Java Foundation Classes (JFC). Swing includes graphical user interface (GUI) widgets such as text boxes, buttons, split-panes, and tables.\n\nSwing widgets provide more sophisticated GUI components than the earlier Abstract Windowing Toolkit. Since they are written in pure Java, they run the same on all platforms, unlike the AWT which is tied to the underlying platform's windowing system. Swing supports pluggable look and feel – not by using the native platform's facilities, but by roughly emulating them. This means you can get any supported look and feel on any platform. The disadvantage of lightweight components is possibly slower execution. The advantage is uniform behavior on all platforms.

Question: what was the cause of the twin towers to collapse?
Answer: The twin towers did not collapsed because the stee. melted because the fire wasn't hot enough to melt steel. They collapsed becaue the steel columns that held up the buildings buckled. When steel is exposed to high temperatures for an extended period of time, its elastic modulus (or stiffness) decreases at a very fast rate. It is believed that the protective fire coating was blown off the steel at the initial impact, causing the steel to be exposed to higher temperatures for a longer period of time. \n\nThe steel columns in the building were connected by trusses that were supposed to support their own weight, the weight of the concrete floors, and the weight of all the office equipment. The high temperature damaged the material and one floor collapsed onto another. Once the first floor collapsed, all the floor above it lost their support and fell.

Question: MY heart pulse gets up to 250 after bending over just the right way , whats wrong with me?
Answer: I would question how you are recording a pulse of 250 beats per minute...its roughly 4 beats per second.  I have seen patients with that sort of heart rate and it feels like the pulse is vibrating rather than beating.  Even with a stethoscope it was impossible to count the heart rate.  Only with the use of EKG equipment did we get an actual accounting of the heart rate.  Secondly it is very unlikely that your heart is beating like that and you are not symptomatic in any way (lightheadedness, shortness of breath, nearly passing out, chest pain).  I'm not saying it couldn't happen but it doesn't exactly add up.  

ADDENDUM:  You say you are getting 64 beats in 15 seconds - as I said above, I have tried to take someone's pulse whose heart was moving that fast and could not discern a pulse.  At that rate your heart does not have time to fill with blood to even produce a full pulse.

The EKG's you had were static, that is you were not moving.  You do need a work up by a cardiologist.  There is a test called a tilt table that can replicate the action of you bending over while you are hooked up to the monitoring equipment.  I would bet this is a supraventricular tachycardia.  If it is there is a procedure - ablation therapy - that can complete cure the problem for life without medication.  Until then there are medications that can control the rate.  Good luck.
